GDP year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter, unemployment and current account as a percentage of GDP for the ten OECD members are taken from the cache's point-in-time vintage store as visible on 2026-10-01, so they are what was published rather than today's revision. Headline and core inflation come from national and aggregated sources dated August 2026 in most cases, because core inflation is not in the cache at all. Singapore has no OECD vintages: its GDP year-on-year of 5.70%, unemployment of 1.90% and current account of 16.70% of GDP are web-sourced and its quarter-on-quarter GDP could not be sourced and is recorded as null rather than estimated.

PPP methodology. OECD purchasing power parity rates could not be retrieved, so the PPP deviation table uses World Bank PPP conversion factors for GDP for 2025 (local currency units per international dollar), with Germany as the euro-area proxy because the euro-area aggregate is null in that series - the same convention the pipeline uses for the EUR 10-year yield. Fair values are computed as the ratio of the peer's conversion factor to Australia's and compared with the 2026-09-29 market rate. The Japanese and Singaporean deviations of +58.4% and +57.9% are dominated by Balassa-Samuelson price-level effects and are reported for completeness rather than as tradeable signals. Best available, flagged: the World Bank API at citation [40] read-timed-out at the Phase 6 gate, so the AUD conversion factor of 1.398943 and every other row of the ten-row PPP table could not be re-confirmed against the source; the whole table rests on that one unverified read.

Carry and carry-to-volatility convention. Carry is the policy-rate differential in basis points. Carry-to-volatility is stated as carry in per cent divided by the pair's 60-day realised volatility in per cent, read directly from realisedVol in the cache's derived per-pair files rather than estimated, recomputed, or built from two USD legs. AUD/SGD has no carry-to-volatility ratio because Singapore has no policy rate. Breakeven moves are computed as the annualised differential applied to spot, scaled by 30/365.

Positioning divergence. The CFTC legacy non-commercial net short of 46,814 contracts and the disaggregated leveraged-fund net long of 58,726 contracts are for the same 22 September report date and cannot be reconciled from the sources available. Both are reported. The schema's leveraged-fund and asset-manager fields carry the disaggregated cache figures; the legacy measure is carried in other_positioning_signals. Factor 4 confidence is set at 52 tactical and 48 strategic in consequence, and the net-all-specs percentile of 35 is estimated against the currency brief's plus-or-minus 80,000-contract reversal threshold rather than computed from a full history.

Volatility percentile limitation. The cache's implied-volatility history begins on 2026-08-21, so a one-year implied-volatility percentile for AUD/USD cannot be computed and is a documented gap. The reported figure of 96 is the position of the current 7.547% within the 25 observations of approximately one-month tenor available in that six-week window, whose range is 6.21% to 7.71%. It should be read as a six-week percentile, not a one-year one. The BIS real effective exchange rate percentile of 90 is likewise an estimate anchored on the +9.97% one-year change, because the cached snapshot carries a single period.

Documented data gaps. The following framework-required or desirable figures could not be sourced from a real citable source and are stated as gaps rather than estimated: 3-month EUR/USD, JPY/USD and AUD/USD cross-currency basis quotes, for which the CME calendar roll premium of -46.3bp annualised is used as a partial proxy that bundles the rate differential with the basis; the SOFR-IORB spread; the Australian sovereign CDS spread; AOFM issuance detail and Australian state-government debt figures; the Citi Economic Surprise Index for Australia; FXA and AUD ETF flows; premium hard coking coal and lithium or spodumene spot prices; Chinese CSI 300 and Hang Seng levels, total social financing growth, property indicators and 2026 stimulus amounts; rolling correlation coefficients for AUD against iron ore, the S&P 500, copper and the CSI 300, for which the divergence is established from levels and one-year changes instead; Japanese investor flows into Australian bonds; and a fresh citable AUD seasonality study for October to March.

Figures flagged as best available. The JKM LNG level of approximately USD 24.36 per mmbtu for 2026-09-29 comes from a price-page headline whose body could not be retrieved. The sell-side AUD/USD consensus range of 0.72-0.74 and Westpac's targets of 0.72 for 2026 and 0.73 for 2027 come from article headlines whose bodies returned HTTP 403. Australian ratings and fiscal metrics - triple-A from all three agencies with stable outlooks, net debt of 18.8% of GDP and an underlying cash balance of -1.6% of GDP - rest on a ratings aggregator and a data aggregator rather than on Treasury or agency primary documents. Each is presented as best available and flagged, not as confirmed.

Brent price discrepancy. Two real sources eight sessions apart give materially different Brent levels: USD 114.89 on 2026-09-22 from the cache's FRED series and USD 98.03 on 2026-09-30 from a market data provider. Both are reported with their dates and the roughly 15% retracement is treated as a genuine move driven by recovering Middle East export volumes and the announced release of up to 40 million barrels from the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve, not as a data error. Phase 6 verification added two qualifications. First, the citation [17] figures of 98.03, +8.33% on the month and +50.01% on the year are the values as captured on 2026-09-30; the live page now reads 97.69, +7.95% and +49.48%, so the capture timestamp is stated wherever those figures appear and the one-year change is reported as approximately 50%. Second, citation [18] carries a third level, USD 102.59 for 2026-09-29, which sits between the cache and the market-data provider; it is a news-article reference price for a different session and is not reconciled to either series, so it is reported as a divergence rather than used. Factor 5 tactical confidence is lowered from 55 to 50 in consequence.

Scenario probabilities and expected values. Scenario probabilities are our own assessments and sum to 100% on each horizon. Expected values are the probability-weighted sums of the three outcomes and are stated in pips from the 0.6987 spot. The tactical expected value is approximately +75 pips and the strategic approximately -37 pips. Risk-reward ratios are base case against downside case, with the upside-tail ratio reported separately where the two differ materially.

Weighted score construction. Stance scores are +1 for Bullish, 0 for Neutral and -1 for Bearish, multiplied by confidence divided by 100 and then by the horizon weight from framework v2.0, and summed. The tactical net is +0.3040 and the strategic net is +0.0307. Conviction bands used are: absolute value below 0.10 Neutral, 0.10 to 0.25 conviction 2, 0.25 to 0.45 conviction 3, 0.45 to 0.65 conviction 4 and above 0.65 conviction 5. These bands are the pipeline's own convention and are stated so the mapping is reproducible.

Phase 6 verification pass and corrections. The verification gate for this cycle tested 23 of the 40 citations: 22 resolved, citation 40 failed with a World Bank API read timeout, and citation 6 resolved but did not support the claim attached to it. Seven findings were applied to this dossier after it had been built and had passed the validator, as surgical corrections rather than a rebuild. One, the United States 10-year is standardised on the pipeline cache DGS10 close of 5.24% at 2026-09-28 in place of 5.29%, which moves the AU-US 10-year spread from +9bp to +14bp. Two, the Australian 10-year is standardised on the 5.38% 2026-09-26 cross-section in place of a 5.35% 2026-09-30 close, which moves the 2s10s from +37bp to +40bp. Three, the August monthly CPI headline is detached from citation 6, which is the ABS June 2026 quarterly release and contains no August data, and is flagged as best available on the pipeline calendar event store at Data-Cache/calendar/events/2026-09.csv, occurrence 557807; no citable ABS Monthly Consumer Price Index Indicator page for August 2026 could be retrieved, and no URL was invented. Four, the citation 17 Brent figures are timestamped to their 2026-09-30 capture, the one-year change is reported as approximately 50%, and the citation 18 level of USD 102.59 for 2026-09-29 is recorded as an unreconciled third value. Five, the clause claiming spot traded below 0.70000 for the first time in two months is removed, because the cache's own 2026-09-29 close of 0.6987 is already below 0.70. Six, citation 19 is labelled explicitly as the Q2 2026 reference period, published 2026-07-15 and outside both the 30-day tactical and 60-day strategic freshness windows, with the current-conditions read leaning on the September NBS PMI at citation 20. Seven, the sixteen-of-eighteen participant count and the 4.1% median dot are re-attributed to the September FOMC Summary of Economic Projections and dot plot at citation 26, with the chase.com commentary at citation 27 retained only as a secondary reference. Four further figures are recorded as best available and flagged, with no replacement invented: the RBA Trade-Weighted Index of 64.8 at 2026-09-29 (citation 3), which the live page can no longer confirm because it shows only 64.7 for 30 September and carries no retrievable historical column; the World Bank PPP conversion factors including AUD 1.398943 (citation 40), whose API read timed out and on which the entire ten-row PPP table rests; the AUD/USD forward points (citation 22), whose page resolves un-paywalled at spot 0.6948 with 1-month points of -3.273 and 3-month of -9.059 but whose derived carry figures could not be tied to specific page values; and the JKM level of approximately USD 24.36 per mmbtu together with the 0.72-0.74 sell-side consensus range, both headline-only and already disclosed above. Two items were checked and are not findings: the description of the 29 September RBA decision as unanimous is supported by the media release, which states that the decision was unanimous, and the JPY 1.25% and NOK 4.50% overrides of the cache's monthly CBPOL series are correct and are disclosed in assumption 2. Tactical confidence was lowered at the gate for Factor 1 from 68 to 62, Factor 2 from 55 to 50 and Factor 5 from 55 to 50. Those reductions were applied after scoring.
